skill.name: backend-atomic-commit
skill.description: Strict backend pre-commit and atomic commit guidance for Django and Python repositories. It checks changed files, local quality gates, typing, tests, and commit readiness.
skill.summary: Prepare Django backend changes for clean pre-commit checks and atomic commits.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around commands, paths, labels, and review examples. Two shell command examples are confirmed because they use unquoted command substitution to build ty arguments from git output. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unquoted shell command substitution in ty examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace the examples with a NUL-safe file collection method or an explicit quoted array, and handle the empty file list case.

remediation.issue: Command execution trust boundary is implicit
remediation.suggestion: State that repository scripts, hooks, and test commands should run only in trusted checkouts or after reviewing them.

content.value_statement: Backend commits often fail because local checks, typing, tests, and commit scope drift apart. This skill guides focused fixes, runs relevant gates, and reports commit readiness clearly.
actual_capabilities: Scopes staged, unstaged, and untracked files before checking backend changes.
Runs or recommends Ruff, ty, Django checks, pytest subsets, and pre-commit hooks.
Uses repository AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and .security helper scripts when present.
Applies safe formatting, import, typing, logging, and test cleanup in pre-commit mode.
Evaluates whether staged changes form one coherent atomic commit.
Drafts concise ticket-prefixed commit messages without adding tool signatures.
limitations: It assumes a Python or Django backend workflow and may be less useful for other stacks.
It depends on local tools, scripts, settings, and test data being available.
It can modify files in pre-commit mode, so review diffs before committing.
It does not replace human review for product behavior, migrations, or security impact.

use_cases.title: Clean Backend Changes Before Review
use_cases.description: Run focused formatting, linting, typing, and test checks before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Verify Commit Scope
use_cases.description: Check whether staged files represent one coherent change and identify work that should split out.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Fixes
use_cases.description: Confirm urgent Django fixes pass relevant local gates before a controlled release commit.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Pre-Commit Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when your working tree has backend edits that need local cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run backend-atomic-commit in pre-commit mode. Fix safe lint, format, import, typing, and logging issues in changed backend files. Summarize fixes and remaining blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Check Staged Commit Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after staging files for one planned backend commit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run backend-atomic-commit in atomic-commit mode for my staged files. Check atomicity, required gates, and propose a ticket-prefixed commit message only if ready.

prompt_templates.title: Strict Django Quality Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for risky Django model, migration, API, or test changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the strict Django backend checks. Prioritize repository rules, .security helpers, Ruff, ty, Django checks, targeted tests, migrations, and multi-tenant correctness.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Review Gate Simulation
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before requesting final review on complex backend changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my staged and unstaged backend changes as a reviewer. Separate blocking issues, should-fix items, nits, skipped checks, unsafe assumptions, and any non-atomic changes.

output_examples.input: Run a pre-commit cleanup for changed Django files.
output_examples.output: A concise report listing fixes applied, checks run, remaining issues, and files that still need review.

output_examples.input: Check whether staged backend changes are ready to commit.
output_examples.output: A readiness verdict with gate results, atomicity notes, blocking items, and a proposed human-readable commit subject.

output_examples.input: Review a risky migration and related model changes.
output_examples.output: A risk-focused summary covering migration safety, test coverage, Django checks, and recommended next actions.

best_practices: Run it from the repository root so local rules and helper scripts are discoverable.
Review every file edit and command result before staging or committing changes.
Use atomic-commit mode only after staging files for one logical change.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to bundle unrelated refactors, fixes, and documentation changes into one commit.
Do not skip failed local gates because the same checks are likely to fail in CI.
Do not run repository scripts from untrusted checkouts without reviewing them first.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It checks readiness and proposes a commit message, but the user remains responsible for committing.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits Django and Python backend repositories with Ruff, ty, pytest, pre-commit, and local repository rules.

faq.question: Can it edit source files?
faq.answer: Yes. In pre-commit mode it may apply safe fixes for formatting, imports, typing, logging, and tests.

faq.question: What happens if a required tool is missing?
faq.answer: It reports the missing tool or hook and explains whether that blocks commit readiness.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: It runs or recommends targeted tests when changes are risky and the local environment supports them.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review repository scripts and hooks before allowing local commands to run.
